title: Rank scores without touching the caller's array

blocks.text: A method that changes an object it was passed changes the caller's object. When the caller did not ask for that, it is a bug that shows up far from the method. A method that only needs to read its input works on a copy.
Write `ranked(int[] scores)` in `Ranking`. It returns a new array holding the scores from highest to lowest, and leaves the caller's array exactly as it was:

items: `ranked(new int[]{70, 95, 80})` is `{95, 80, 70}`, and the caller's array is still `{70, 95, 80}`;

cases.says: The result is a new array, even when the scores are already in order.

concepts: Changes a method makes to an object it was passed affect the original, so a method that must not change its input works on a copy.
